title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The monomorphism claim for D_{α,α''} → D_α × D_{α''} holds for a normal-crossings divisor on a manifold. There, a point of the deeper normalized stratum determines its branches, and the map is an injective immersion. For M̄_{g,ν}, which is an orbifold/stack, strata have automorphisms (e.g. symmetric self-intersection branches). In that setting the map into the product is not obviously a monomorphism, and the determination of (167) via (168) needs either a fine-moduli level structure or a stacky reformulation. The page does not address this, though the restriction 'd'abord dans le contexte des espaces analytiques' suggests awareness.
The machine transcription writes D_α for the arrow space and D_{αα} for its pairs; the image and the next page show D_* (objects) and D_{**} (arrows). This is notational, not mathematical.
The reference '(168)' in 'qui figurent dans (168)' probably should be (166), where the maps D_{α,α',α''} ⇉ D_α, D_{α''} are listed.

ideas.what: Defining the composite incidence D_{α,α',α''} → D_{α,α''} via a monomorphism D_{α,α''} → D_α × D_{α''} and the projections to the outer strata
ideas.modern_name: composition in the category of strata of a normal crossings divisor (functoriality of normalized strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. Deligne (Hodge II, 1971) for the semi-simplicial system of normalized intersections

ideas.what: Encoding the boundary stratification of the moduli space as an internal category in analytic spaces (objects = points of normalized strata, arrows = specializations/branches), graded by codimension, with arrows only decreasing codimension and only identities in equal codimension
ideas.modern_name: analytic category of strata / exit-path category made internal; Reedy-type directed category object; analytic analogue of the Artin fan or boundary complex of a toroidal/log space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Exit paths: MacPherson, Treumann (2009), Lurie (Higher Algebra A.6). Boundary complex of M̄_{g,n} as a colimit over strata: Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne (2015). Artin fans: Abramovich–Wise and others (2010s).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions the 'structure à l'infini' of the Teichmüller tower and stratified 'dévissage' ideas, but not, to my knowledge, this internal-category formalism

ideas.what: Internal category in a category of spaces, defined via S-valued points forming a category
ideas.modern_name: internal category / category object (Ehresmann); functor-of-points definition
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 / FGA (group and category objects via functor of points)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formalizes the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν} as a codimension-graded, directed internal category of analytic spaces. This is a geometric enhancement of the combinatorial category of strata (stable graphs) that later underlies tropical moduli (Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne), Artin fans in log geometry, and modular operad gluing structures (Getzler–Kapranov). Here the stratum spaces themselves, not just their combinatorial indices, are the objects. This links the analytic tubular/boundary structure directly to a category object whose nerve is a simplicial analytic space.
missed.quote: Une "structure de déploiement à l'infini … modulaire" sera définie d'abord une structure de "catégorie analytique" 𝒟 i.e. d'une catégorie dans la catégorie des espaces analytiques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers an early axiomatic framework, an internal stratified category with codimension grading, for boundary strata of moduli spaces. It is comparable to modern exit-path/Artin-fan formalisms and could inform a historical attribution of the 'category of strata as a geometric object' viewpoint.

missed.claim: The definition of a modular 'structure à l'infini' is begun here as an abstract notion. The page indicates it is to be developed first analytically and presumably later in other contexts (algebraic, stacky). Whether the abstract notion was completed or applied to the Teichmüller tower in this manuscript is unclear from this page.
missed.quote: (d'abord dans le contexte des espaces analytiques)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An algebraic or stacky version would need to handle automorphisms of strata, which is exactly where the monomorphism argument breaks. This is a natural point of contact with modern log/tropical moduli theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The ingredients are individually standard (internal categories, normalized strata of normal crossings divisors, codimension-directed categories). Packaging the boundary of M_{g,ν} as a graded internal analytic category of strata is a nice, apparently unpublished axiomatization that anticipates later strata-category formalisms. However, it is a definitional set-up rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: Arrow-space notation: 'D_α ——— flèches' should be 'D_{**} ——— flèches'; 'D_{αα}' should be 'D_{**}'; objects are 'D_*' (asterisks, not alphas), consistent with the next page.
'disjointement' is likely 'déploiement' (or similar); the title reads roughly 'Une "structure de déploiement à l'infini" (?) … modulaire', reading uncertain.
'est un mono Ex' should probably read 'est un mono[morphisme], et'.
In '(D_{**}, b) ×_{D_*} (D_{**}, s)' the subscript is D_*, not D_α.
Top line: page number '56'; references in the first lines appear to be (167) and (168), with the last reference likely (166) or (168) (overwritten).
